$comment: CuratorGuard policy for the Vetro Lagoon curator Safe (Ethereum). Derived from the Safe's executed history (nonces 0-30: NAV updates, settles, approve(vault) per asset, MultiSendCallOnly v1.4.1 batches). Apply with: npx hardhat curator-guard-sync --network ethereum --guard <CuratorGuard> --policy policies/curator-guard/vetro-lagoon.ethereum.json --proposer <governance Safe> [--allow-unlock], then --execute after the timelock delay (on today's chain the first sync also needs a NAV band on the funded entries or --allow-unconstrained-nav, docs section 7.2 step 1). Owner management (addOwnerWithThreshold, changeThreshold, setGuard) is NOT allowlisted: the council (owner management, disableModule, setFallbackHandler(0), the empty rejection) or the admin (setGuard, setModuleGuard, enableModule, any other handler, batches) approves each such one-off with approveTransaction (safeTxGas is free: a failed approved execution reverts the whole Safe transaction either way, docs section 7.5). mode may only be Lockdown or Enforced: Bypass is an incident action on the guard, never a desired state.
$comment_nav: updateNewTotalAssets is marked unconstrained ONLY because the vaults are unfunded: before any debtRatio above zero, either the Lagoon-level controls of docs section 8 are live (whitelist mode, guardrails, valuation / security-council roles at Vetro) or each funded vault gets a NAV band here (GreaterThanOrEqual + LessThanOrEqual on word 0 around the settled NAV, re-synced with every funding step) on updateNewTotalAssets AND, with the same bounds, on settleDeposit and settleRedeem: a settle repeats whatever mark is pending (the vault reverts WrongNewTotalAssets otherwise), a securityCouncil mark included once that role sits outside the Safe (review G11b-2). settleDeposit also settles pending redeems, so the two settle entries are one custody exit: a responder narrows both or the target (review G11b-1). The guard cannot judge a NAV: with these five entries alone a colluding signer quorum can mark a vault down, buy in, mark it up and redeem the whole custody in one transaction.
$comment_handler: The Safe currently runs the canonical CompatibilityFallbackHandler v1.4.1 (0xfd07...Ec99), which implements EIP-1271: a signer quorum could authorise USDC permit / transferWithAuthorization off-chain and bypass the guard. Policy traffic is refused until the signers execute the Vetro-approved setFallbackHandler(0x0). See docs/curator-guard.md section 7.
$comment_settlement_deadline: Before a public vault is funded, deploy contracts/helpers/SettlementDeadline.sol, add { target: <its address>, signature: assertBefore(uint256) } here (a plain call, no rules) and have the signers put assertBefore(deadline) FIRST in every settlement batch: a confirmed batch nobody executed before its deadline then reverts for every executor instead of staying a public option on a stale mark (review G13e-1). The sync refuses that entry unless the code at the address is this repository's SettlementDeadline build: a look-alike that dispatches assertBefore and never reverts would bind nothing (review G16c-1).
$comment_guardians: Narrow-only responders for THIS Safe (lockdown, revoke, revokeAllApprovals): fill in Vetro's monitoring bot / on-call keys before go-live. Deployment-wide responders hold GUARDIAN_ROLE on the guard instead (granted through the timelock) and are not listed here. A replacement guard starts with none, so re-sync it with this file before the signers switch to it.
$comment_unwrappers: The three canonical MultiSendCallOnly deployments (v1.3.0, v1.4.1, v1.5.0): same hash-pinned, storage-free code, so registering all three costs no trust and keeps batching alive when a wallet switches library.
